critical_code_review_comments: scan_tracks.is_bass triggers when `mean < 55` even on genuinely melodic alto/tenor-range tracks (e.g., a vocal line that dips low). Baby1's Tenor Sax mean sits around 59 so it survives, but future songs with a melodic bassoon/baritone/alto range near 54-55 could be unfairly demoted. Consider only applying the bass penalty when BOTH register AND (name OR GM 32-39) agree, OR when mean <= 50.
fisher_price.py is now ~1260 lines — still past the 700-line split threshold called out in iter13. Scoring heuristics would read better as a separate melody_score() helper.
The GM-program bass window `32 <= progs[0] <= 39` only looks at the first program_change; multi-program tracks (common in GM1 arrangements) can hide a bass program behind a later change.

rca of the issue: Previous bug: scan_tracks.melody_score didn't penalise bass register, so GM 32-39 (Pick Bass etc.) could tie or beat the real lead on multi-instrument MIDIs — the auto-selected track ended up being whichever got the best variety/density, often the bass. Fix (fisher_price.py scan_tracks): compute `is_bass = 'bass' in name/instrument label OR GM 32-39 OR mean pitch < 55`; if is_bass then score *= 0.4. Also +20 for name hints melody/lead/vocal/voice/sing/solo/tune/main. Verified: baby1 Pick Bass dropped to 31.3 (vs Tenor Sax 84.4), whoscheating Ac.Bass dropped to 34.2 (vs Jazz GT. 76.0).
